answer: I would tie each agent to one taxi medallion. First, the agent buys a city medallion and pins its number to its public key. Second, the network checks the city registry and bars a second agent on that medallion. Third, a yearly recheck demands a fresh renewal receipt, or the seat freezes. Fielding 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 medallions at $80,000 each, $80 million before one fake earns a cent. You can forge a tin badge in an afternoon, but a real medallion needs a city clerk and a background check. Yarrow grows on any roadside in a week; a medallion is jade, slow to cut and hard to fake.
